subject: Medicine
summary: Guillain‑Barré syndrome is an acute, immune‑mediated polyneuropathy that typically follows an infection. It presents with rapidly ascending weakness, areflexia, and possible autonomic dysfunction, potentially leading to respiratory failure.

sections.p: GBS is defined by progressive limb weakness, loss of reflexes, and a history of recent infection. Diagnosis relies on clinical criteria, nerve conduction studies, and CSF analysis.
b: Clinical criteria: progressive weakness, areflexia, recent infection

t.b: Shows demyelination or axonal loss; confirms peripheral neuropathy and helps subtype.
Elevated protein with normal cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation); supports diagnosis when clinical picture is unclear.

t.a: Serology for Campylobacter jejuni, CMV, EBV, HIV
t.b: Identifies likely trigger; positive results guide prognosis.

sections.p: The Hughes Functional Grading Scale stages GBS from 0 (normal) to 6 (death). It guides monitoring and treatment urgency.
b: Stage 1: mild weakness, no respiratory involvement
Stage 3: significant weakness, possible respiratory compromise
Stage 5: severe weakness, ventilatory support required

sections.p: The most common trigger is a preceding infection, especially Campylobacter jejuni. Other infections and conditions common in low‑resource settings also contribute.
Patients develop symmetrical ascending weakness, areflexia, and may have sensory disturbances. Autonomic instability can cause blood pressure swings and cardiac arrhythmias.
b: Weakness starts in feet and ascends

sections.p: Urgent signs include rapid progression to respiratory failure, severe autonomic instability, or cranial nerve involvement. Complications can be fatal.

sections.p: Treat the underlying trigger if identified, provide supportive care, and consider immunotherapy. Monitor respiratory function closely.
b: Supportive care: bed rest, physiotherapy, monitoring of vitals

sections.p: Patients need long‑term follow‑up for residual weakness and autonomic dysfunction. Prevention focuses on infection control and early treatment of infections.
Differential diagnoses include myasthenia gravis, botulism, tick‑borne paralysis, and metabolic neuropathies.

whenToSeekHelp: Rapidly worsening weakness, difficulty breathing, severe autonomic instability, or bulbar muscle involvement
